title: jevgrep
brief: Find code by asking what it does: a CLI (plus an installable agent skill) that uses Jev to judge relevance across folders, files, and declarations, returning relevant files, reading leads, and verbatim source excerpts in one stdout response. Installs with `npm install -g @dzhng/jevgrep`; its own ten-task SWE-bench comparison claims ~30% lower coding-agent cost at equal task success. (~803 stars, MIT.) Cost figures are author-reported and not independently verified.
caveat: Installs with `npm install -g @dzhng/jevgrep`; its own ten-task SWE-bench comparison claims ~30% lower coding-agent cost at equal task success. (~803 stars, MIT.) Cost figures are author-reported and not independently verified.
details: jevgrep is a CLI for coding agents that finds code by asking what it does: run `jg "How are telemetry events recorded and sent?" ./my-project` and it returns relevant files, reading leads, and verbatim source excerpts in one stdout response. It uses the Jev relevance engine to judge relevance across folders, files, and declarations (Python, TypeScript/JavaScript, Go, and Rust get declaration parsing), exploring the repo hierarchy rather than forcing results into a fixed top-k list. The pitch is cost: in their ten-task SWE-bench comparison it solved the same 8 of 10 tasks as the baseline at ~30% lower coding-agent cost. Requires Node 22+ and a key for Vercel AI Gateway, TypeSafe, OpenRouter, OpenCode Zen, or a TypeSafe-compatible endpoint; install the companion agent skill too (`jg skill`), since the CLI alone doesn't teach your agent to use it. MIT, from dzhng; searches send eligible source content to Jev, so choose a search root you intend to share.
